resources.string: Use an existing router or portable Wi-Fi. Keep the iPhone and car on the same network with Internet access.
Existing Wi-Fi · Keep both devices on the same Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on. No car hotspot is needed.

Connect the car and iPhone to the same external Wi-Fi in system settings. Enter its exact name and WPA2 password below; leave the password empty only for an open network. Use WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode and disable client isolation on the router. DiPlay keeps this Wi-Fi connection and creates no hotspot.

An independent CarPlay receiver for Android head units. Wired and wireless connections run on the head unit, with local authentication. A standard iPhone can connect without a jailbreak, Mac, dongle or sign-in.\n\nThis preview uses an experimental accessory identity. Compatibility with every iPhone and head unit is still being tested. It is not an Apple-certified product.

Return from car settings to DiPlay, then connect. Accept the CarPlay prompt on your iPhone. A car internet plan is not required; mobile data availability depends on your phone’s network settings.

DiPlay draws this card on the map. Move it in 2 % steps. The iOS glass card cannot be moved on its own. Changes apply without reconnecting. The custom card stays on for straight-ahead as well as turns.
Keep the home-screen map in sync with the dashboard
On: the home-screen card mirrors the dashboard map. Off: hide the home-screen card so only the instrument cluster shows that map. This does not change CarPlay’s own main screen.
With Report location to iPhone on, DiPlay also sends the car\'s wheel speed and gear, so Apple Maps can keep your position moving in tunnels and car parks. Reconnects CarPlay.

Dashboard map on the centre screen
Requests CarPlay secondary map stream (Stream 111) for center screen floating card and launcher widget embedding on head units without a digital instrument cluster screen.
Shows a 16:9 floating map card on the center screen with natural proportions and pinch-to-zoom support.

Auto-hide when leaving home screen: Not active. Grant Usage Access via ADB or Accessibility service.

While DiPlay is in the background, the dashboard map also shows as a card on the home screen: BYD home, map home or your default launcher. Tap the card to open CarPlay, drag it to move it, and pinch it to resize it. The dashboard keeps its map. Needs permission to draw over other apps.
Draw over other apps: not allowed. Allow it in the app settings, or over ADB: adb shell appops set %1$s SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow
This head unit has no settings screen for this permission. Allow it over ADB.
Share the live map with other launchers

Launchers that support DiPlay can show the live dashboard map inside their own home screen. Off by default, because any app on the head unit could then ask for the map. See docs/LAUNCHER_INTEGRATION.md.

Full-screen app area; swipe right from the left edge to reveal the app dock
Disable rounded corner clipping on the CarPlay display; use on rectangular head-unit screens where edges get cut off. Applies at the next connection.
Where CarPlay shows its apps, clock and status. Between Driver\'s side and Bottom it moves at once; Automatic leaves it to the iPhone and applies after a reconnect.
CarPlay in the head unit\'s split screen

When the head unit shows DiPlay in split screen, CarPlay redraws for that window instead of shrinking with black bars, and back to full screen without reconnecting. The window\'s size is learned the first time, so the picture fits exactly from the next connection. With the dock on Automatic, CarPlay then puts it at the bottom. Applies at the next connection.
Turn CarPlay with the screen without reconnecting

For head units whose screen turns. CarPlay gets a square picture holding a landscape and a portrait screen, so turning the screen redraws CarPlay instead of reconnecting. A larger square can increase video work and reduce smoothness, especially with Sharper on a large screen. If you rarely turn the screen, leaving this off may help. The custom safe area does not apply to a square picture. Applies at the next connection.

Steering-wheel call keys answer and end CarPlay calls. On the Guangqi head unit the call key answers, the hang-up key ends or declines, and a short or long press on the voice key opens Siri; while CarPlay is connected the car\'s own call screen stays hidden and the car\'s voice assistant and wake word are paused. On DiLink 3 the keys are not yet verified. Vehicle testing is still required. Disabled by default; dashboard call cards are a separate setting.

CarPlay can move to two thirds of the screen while DiPlay shows a panel in the rest: on the passenger\'s side of a landscape screen, at the bottom of a portrait one (clock and, where it is read, the battery). Show and hide it from the in-session menu. Applies at the next connection.
Apps that support it, such as Apple Music, send up to about two minutes of music ahead, so short Wi-Fi gaps are not heard. Other apps keep the normal stream. Reconnects CarPlay.
CarPlay audio over the car\'s Bluetooth (experimental)

DiPlay offers the iPhone no CarPlay audio, so music, navigation and calls should go over the iPhone\'s Bluetooth connection with the car. Keep the iPhone paired with the car and choose Bluetooth as the car\'s audio source. If the sound plays on the iPhone instead, turn this off. Reconnects CarPlay.

An external USB Bluetooth adapter is plugged in. The adapter itself cannot play audio — this feature sends sound over the iPhone\'s Bluetooth connection with the car\'s own Bluetooth. If the car\'s Bluetooth cannot play audio (the reason most people use an adapter), turning this on will leave you with no sound at all.
Tries to reduce speaker echo sent to the other person during CarPlay calls. Results depend on the head unit. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.
Cuts bass from CarPlay call audio. This may change how voices sound. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.

Uses the standard car microphone input (MIC) and skips communication audio mode switching during calls. Fixes silent microphone on Allwinner and other head units during WeChat or phone calls. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.

Shows each main-screen CarPlay frame at the time the iPhone stamped on it plus a short delay, instead of as soon as it is decoded. The delay adjusts itself so that most frames are decoded in time; frames still not ready by their time are shown at once. Scrolling can look more even, but touches respond later. Picture adjustments do not apply. Reconnects CarPlay.

CarPlay shows this icon and name in its app list. Tap it to return to the car\'s own screen. Changes apply the next time CarPlay connects. Custom images are automatically resized to at most 512×512 pixels and 256 KB.
Saved. CarPlay shows the new icon and name the next time it connects.
This head unit has no image picker.
Size of text and controls on DiPlay\'s own screens. Automatic enlarges them on large screens with a low density. CarPlay is not affected.

Uses native SurfaceView hardware overlays directly instead of TextureView, bypassing GPU View composition and significantly reducing GPU/memory load on low-end car headunits (e.g. Android 4.4/6.0, MT3561, T3). Picture adjustments do not apply. Reconnects CarPlay.
Head unit has no native Bluetooth adapter; wireless CarPlay unavailable. Please use a wired USB cable.
iPhone USB is busy or occupied by another app (e.g. car iPod player). Close the car iPod app and reconnect the cable.
The iPhone is not responding to USB configuration requests (its USB state is stuck). Unplug the cable, restart the iPhone, reconnect it, and then tap Retry.
iPhone USB permission was not granted. Check for system permission prompts, exit any car iPod app, and reconnect.
Declares the car’s native Bluetooth MAC to iPhone for proper audio routing. Reconnect to apply.
Enter the car’s native Bluetooth MAC address (e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF). Find it in iPhone Settings → Bluetooth → (i) or your car’s Bluetooth settings.
Please enter a valid 12-digit hexadecimal MAC address.

For old chips (e.g. MTK 8227L): while reversing, the video decoder is fully released; 2.5 s after reverse exit it cold-starts and requests a fresh keyframe. Enable only if reverse exit black-screens on your unit.
Direct hardware stack for external USB dongles (e.g. UGREEN CM591/CM390, Realtek, Actions ATS2851) to run wireless CarPlay.
No external USB Bluetooth adapter detected — plug in a compatible USB dongle.
USB permission required — tap to request access
Bluetooth pairing request from %1$s.\nConfirm the number matches your iPhone:

USB Bluetooth diagnostic: tests adapter permissions and HCI hardware, then restores the wireless service. Disconnect CarPlay before testing. A hardware pass does not verify iPhone pairing or CarPlay; save the report after reproducing a connection failure.
Balances each sound inside DiPlay when the head unit has a single volume for everything.
For head units whose system USB list never shows the iPhone: enumerates USB devices directly and opens the device node, which may require root. Applies at the next connection and restarts CarPlay.
Turn off Bluetooth auto-connect while CarPlay is connected (experimental)

While CarPlay is connected by cable or wirelessly, turns off the car\'s global Bluetooth auto-connect so the car does not page the phone again after the phone drops the call link. DiPlay also disconnects the phone from the car\'s Bluetooth, as the car\'s Bluetooth page does. The Bluetooth radio stays on. The previous switch position comes back when the session ends, or the next time DiPlay opens if the app exits abnormally. Has no effect while CarPlay audio over the car\'s Bluetooth is on. Applies at the next connection.
Route the call downlink through the music stream (experimental)

Route the call downlink through the music stream instead of the telephony stream, while call mode and the microphone uplink stay unchanged. Use this only if the call downlink is silent on the telephony stream while media audio works. Applies at the next connection.

While navigation, assistant or call audio is actually playing, lower the media volume inside DiPlay and restore it about a second after the announcement ends. It only affects sound that DiPlay itself plays, and it never changes the system volume. Applies at the next connection.
Bring task to front to dismiss the dock bar (experimental)

Some launchers keep a dock bar over the CarPlay picture, squeezing the window so the picture shrinks with black borders. When DiPlay detects that squeeze, it brings its own task to the front, which makes launchers of this kind drop the bar. The CarPlay screen itself never changes. Applies at the next connection.
2.4 GHz only (channels 1–13). Channel 1 is the most compatible.
Rooted units only: DiPlay starts the system hostapd as root and creates the hotspot itself. Set the name and password below; the iPhone joins this hotspot.
Root hotspot: this head unit must be rooted. DiPlay creates the hotspot itself; keep your iPhone’s Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on.

On the next connection or when DiPlay opens, turn off regular Wi-Fi and start the saved car hotspot. Keep its name and password. For boot startup, also enable “Open after the car starts”. No ADB authorization is needed on this Android 5.1 unit.

On the next connection or when DiPlay opens, turn off regular Wi-Fi and start the saved car hotspot. Keep its name and password. For boot startup, also enable “Open after the car starts”. No ADB authorization is needed on this unit.
Request permanent focus for media instead of letting other players duck CarPlay. Only helps head units that duck CarPlay to silence; it can mute other players. Takes effect on the next connection.
Light or dark for DiPlay\'s own screens. Automatic follows CarPlay\'s day and night setting. CarPlay itself is not affected.
Keeps the car from paging the phone back onto its Bluetooth. Turns off car Bluetooth audio. Applies after reconnecting.
CarPlay sound plays over the car\'s Bluetooth. Turns off the auto-connect switch below. Applies after reconnecting.
Longer is steadier over a weak link but answers later. Applies after reconnecting.
Takes effect at once. Turn off to give the volume keys back to the car.
For testing. Tap: normal restart (svc power reboot). Hold 3 s: immediate restart (setprop sys.powerctl reboot). CarPlay drops and comes back afterwards.
Other ways · not verified on this car, not recommended

The car\'s Wi-Fi is connected to %1$s. Wireless CarPlay uses Wi-Fi Direct on the same single 2.4 GHz radio, and the two connections take turns. The car\'s Wi-Fi will disconnect in %2$d s for a steadier connection; it reconnects when CarPlay ends.

Guangqi units only. How far music drops while a prompt plays, measured from its level before the prompt, so it feels the same at any media volume. The car on its own drops music to one fixed level, which with the iPhone\'s own duck is almost silent at ordinary volumes. Applies from the next prompt.

Guangqi units only. While DiPlay runs, the wheel, panel and knob volume keys set the car\'s media volume through DiPlay, which shows its own volume bar instead of the car\'s. Reversing, calls, the stock voice assistant and the car\'s own navigation keep the car\'s handling. Takes effect at once. After updating DiPlay, restart the car to use the new version.
